review_candidates.description: Can you improve the health of a region? That’s the challenge that you will have if you become the Director of Research & Health for North West Cancer Research. If you live in our region you are up to 25% more likely to experience cancer in your lifetime, more likely to be diagnosed late and sadly you will be more likely to die of cancer than the national average. Those are the statistics that, working with others, we need to change. This is a big job, and a big challenge, but you won’t do it alone. You will work with the CEO, the Trustees and the staff team at North West Cancer Research. You will also have the resources available to put in place your own team. This information pack will tell you more about North West Cancer Research, what we have done in the past, where we are now and what we want to achieve in the future. We have a long track record of funding great research and in recent years we have innovated to start providing education, outreach and information to help people reduce their risk of having cancer, recognise the early symptoms and live with and beyond it. Our campaigns can be eye-catching and trail-blazing, but we also want to be in homes, classrooms and community groups across the region delivering accessible information to people from all backgrounds. We recognise that we can’t do this alone and that the work and resources of one organisation isn’t enough. For this reason, you’ll be an interface between North West Cancer Research and NHS Commissioners, Providers, Public Health Teams and other charities working in the health space. You will have the connections and knowledge to ensure that our work is aligned with the programmes being delivered by others across the region. Finally, we want to connect to patients and patient support groups around the region to understand how we can support them and how we can learn from their valuable experiences. If you are interested in a big challenge, and if you want to make a big difference to our region, then please do read on.

Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement and evidence-led decision-making across the philanthropy portfolio and direct team. review_candidates.description: Suburban Connect is a consortium of global leaders in tunnelling including CPB Contractors, Ghella and Acciona Construction delivering the Tunnels South package on Suburban Rail Loop (SRL) East, on behalf of Suburban Rail Loop Authority (SRLA). SRL East from Cheltenham to Box Hill is now under construction, with tunnelling to start in 2026 and trains to be running by 2035. Suburban Connect is constructing the 16kms of tunnels between Cheltenham and Glen Waverley using 4 tunnel boring machines and a range of excavation methods. The works also include 55 cross passages, 2 tunnel portal structures, 2 station box excavations and associated supports. Co-ordinate site administration and other commercial matters within the zone. Engage with suppliers & subcontractors including maintaining good working relationships to ensure timely resolution of financial issues. Co-ordinate matters concerning project-wide, finance, accounts payable and procurement of goods and services. Good computer literacy skills, knowledge of accounting practices, ability to work in a fast-paced team environment and excellent attention to detail. As a company that values diversity as a source of talent, we work to foster an inclusive environment that promotes respect, belonging and engagement so that all people can participate on an equal opportunity basis. We invite everyone to apply regardless of origin, circumstances, background or condition.

Your Role with us: You'll be a part of our critical distribution operation transporting clothing and homeware products to our stores. Adopt a 'Safety First' mindset where nothing is placed over the safety of yourself, the public, or your colleagues. Most shifts operate on a 5 days out of 7 rota shift pattern. Typical shift patterns shown below including the times you will start between on each band, please make sure when you apply you specify what times you can work between. Elmsall Band A & B (42 hrs) - A - 02:50 - 06:30, B - 06:31 - 10:59 Elmsall Band C & D & E (45 hrs) - C - 11:00 - 17:00, D - 17:01 - 21:29, E - 21:30 - 01:59 Elmsall Part Time Band D & E - Fri/Sat (18 hrs) - D - 17:01 - 21:29, E - 21:30 - 01:59 Dearne Band A (42 hrs) - 04:00 - 08:00 Dearne Band C & D (45hrs) - C - 10:30 - 17:00, D - 17:01 - 23:00 Dearne Part Time C - Sat/Sun (18 hrs) - 10:30-17:00 Dearne Part Time D - Fri/Sat (18 hrs) - 17:01 - 23:00 What You’ll Bring Class 1 C+E license holders with a CPC card Minimum of 1 year Class 1 HGV driving experience including the coupling and uncoupling of trailers Maximum of 6 points on license and no convictions or disqualifications. Following an initial application screen, you will be invited to a driving assessment and interview. About Us You know Next, but did you know we’re a FTSE-100 retail company employing over 44,000 people across the Next group. At the last count we have over 450 stores, plus the Next Online and it’s now possible to buy on-line from over 80 countries around the world! So we’ve gone global!
